# Source criticism (testing documents and reports) (`source_criticism`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/ideas.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Scientific method & philosophical ideas (`ideas`)
- Deps: helped by empiricism_over_authority
- Core idea: A written or oral report is evidence only to the degree that its origin can be examined: who says it, how close were they to the event, what did they gain by saying it, do independent witnesses agree, and is it physically possible. Ten chronicles that copy one another are one witness. Forgeries betray themselves by anachronism: Lorenzo Valla showed in 1440 that the 'Donation of Constantine' uses Latin words, titles and place names that did not exist in Constantine's time. Ibn Khaldun's test is plausibility against how the world works: he challenges a reported Israelite army of over 600,000 by asking whether the territory could sustain so many fighters or allow them to manoeuvre.
- Pitfalls:
  - Applying it aloud to Scripture, hadith, a dynasty's genealogy or a monastery's founding charter; that is heresy, treason or an attack on property titles
  - Arguing from silence: lack of surviving records is weak evidence that something did not happen
  - Assuming older means more reliable, or that a printed or officially sealed text must be true
  - Crediting Valla alone; Nicholas of Cusa (1433) and Reginald Pecock reached the same verdict on the Donation independently
- History: greece: c. 430 BC – Herodotus reports what is said without vouching for it; c. 400 BC Thucydides sets out his rules for testing eyewitnesses (I.20–22); china: c. 90 BC – Sima Qian compares sources and marks doubtful traditions; 710 Liu Zhiji, Shitong, the first treatise on critical historiography; late 17th c. Yan Ruoqu proves parts of the Book of Documents forged (evidential scholarship); islamic: 9th c. – hadith scholars grade reports by examining each chain of transmitters; c. 1030 al-Biruni's India; 1377 Ibn Khaldun, Muqaddimah; europe: 1440 – Valla on the Donation of Constantine (printed 1517); 1681 Mabillon founds the science of dating charters; 1670–1678 Spinoza and Richard Simon apply the method to the Bible; 1820s Ranke
- Read:
  - Lorenzo Valla, De falso credita et ementita Constantini donatione (1440)
  - Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah: An Introduction to History (tr. Franz Rosenthal, 1958)
  - Anthony Grafton, Forgers and Critics: Creativity and Duplicity in Western Scholarship (1990)
